scenes.intro: Hello Samantha. You're about to see your financial picture drawn as a home and your overall score. Your financial health score is 82 out of 100, which Sherpas calls strong. The plan shows your savings and investments run out at age 73 in the projection, so you have strength now but a later-life gap to note.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: This is your plumbing, savings and cash flow, and its state is solid. Your score for this part is 22 out of 30 and the plan shows you run about $6,418 a year short. That means you can cover essentials today, but the shortfall draws on your cash reserve and leaves little slack for near-term college payments.
scenes.pillar_debt: These are your walls, debt, and their state is solid. Your score here is 20 out of 20 and you have no debt: $0 outstanding. In daily life that means no monthly loan payments take your income, so the money you earn is available to fund college or retirement instead.
scenes.pillar_investments: This is your garden, investments, and its state is cracked. Your garden scores 10 out of 15 and $900,000 of your assets is your home. That means a lot of your wealth is not easily spent, so there is less invested money available for near-term college and long-term retirement.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: These are your foundations, cash and emergency fund, and their state is solid. Foundations score 15 out of 15 and your $80,000 of cash covers 7.9 months of essential expenses. In daily life that means you can handle surprises now, though after near-term payments your cushion has little extra slack.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: This is your roof, insurance and protection, and its state is solid. Your roof scores 14 out of 20 and you hold $2,000,000 of term life insurance. For you that cover sits where your household is most exposed and would help replace income for the children if your income stopped.
scenes.move_1: This step closes a coverage gap for your roof; Sherpas already worked it out. It moves your overall score from 82 out of 100 to 84 out of 100 by adding homeowners insurance on your primary home so the coverage gap clears. That change would keep a property or liability claim from tapping your home's equity.
scenes.move_2: This step repairs the garden by spreading out the money you hold in one single fund. The plan moves about $58,300 out of your VTI holding and raises your overall score to 83 out of 100. In daily life that spreads risk so a single fund is less likely to dominate your returns.
scenes.move_3: This step repairs the garden by moving some invested money toward a bit less growth. The plan moves about $17,100 of your invested holdings into slightly less growth and lifts your overall score to 83 out of 100. Concretely, this nudges your portfolio mix so it is a little less dependent on high-growth swings.
scenes.timeline: Look ahead: this timeline shows your house through the years and retirement at 65. On the current plan your savings and investments run out at age 73 in the projection. That means from retirement at 65 the projection shows savings exhausted at 73, so later years would need other income sources to cover planned spending.
